title: LTT 9779 b - The Planet That Answers With Light
narration:
Some planets swallow the light that reaches them.
This one hands it back.
LTT 9779 b is a super-Earth with a permanent gleam.
Its star is quiet. Dim. Easy to overlook.
The planet is not easy to overlook.
It sits close in, and it never gets the chance to cool down.
High above the surface, the sky is made of metal.
Clouds of metal, miles up, doing nothing useful.
The dayside is irradiated. Continuously. Without pause.
Yet the surface never cooks.
Almost none of that light is absorbed.
Nearly all of it is reflected straight back into space.
From a distance, the planet glows like a coin in the dark.
Not a coal. A mirror.
Astronomers measured the brightness and did not believe it.
A number that high usually means a mistake.
They checked. It is one of the most reflective worlds known.
The night side stays dark. The day side burns.
That is the unsettling part.
The hottest worlds should look like ovens.
This one looks like it is smiling.
It orbits a star so mild it barely deserves the name.
And still the planet comes back brilliant.
No surface you could stand on. No sky you could breathe.
You would not survive a single breath up there.
Nothing down there generates its own shine.
It is the brightest warning light in a quiet system.
The gleam is borrowed. And it never stops.
